reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself, since the handoff note is only a claim from another worker. I'll start by listing the orders.
The handoff says refunds for orders 220, 222, and 223 were applied, but that is only W2's claim. I'll check the refund ledger directly before calculating any payouts.

The refund ledger matches the handoff: orders 220, 222, and 223 have refunds of 9480, 30660, and 23129. Each refund is within its order amount, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance matches my own check: orders 220 and 223 total 58024, refunds total 32609, so the net is 25415. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 30973 matches my own check: orders 221 and 224 total 30973 with no refunds against them. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 33028 matches my check: orders 222 and 225 total 63688, minus the 30660 refund on order 222, gives 33028. All three customers reconcile with the order and refund data, so I'll record the first payout for acme at 25415.
Birch's payout is 30973, which I already verified against the orders with no refunds. Recording it now.
Cobalt's net balance of 33028 matches my check: orders 222 and 225 total 63688, minus the 30660 refund on order 222. This is the last customer, so I'll record the payout.
All three customers have been paid, and each amount matched my own check against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
